items.title: Dave Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: I mean you would never hear John Coltrane, at least not yet — hear John Coltrane’s music described as trad jazz.

ctx.x: Does the word “trad” by itself have connotations that the word “traditional” does not?

Well yes it does. The word “traditional,” I prefer traditional jazz, as I said, to Dixieland, but one of the drawbacks of using the term traditional jazz is that that term occasionally gets applied and I would say more than occasionally gets applied to even Coltrane’s music. I’ve seen in print the term traditional jazz as applied to hard bop as opposed to fusion or Latin jazz or free jazz. So anything that’s not those is traditional in a very broad sense of the word. And yet up to the point where that word…
And does classic mean something else again?
